text:
incident-bot: PAGING: runtime-canary-high-latency -> severity=P2. Canary wave 4312 showing sustained p95 increase and throughput drop, kernel-fallbacks spike. Affected region: us-west-2. Impacting a small % of paid traffic.

sam (oncall): On it. pulling up dashboards now — any obvious deploy id?

deploy-bot: rollout event: release/2026.03.17-wave-4312 started at 1849998600. feature_flags: canary_route=v2 ON.

ting (eng-runtime): seeing a lot of calls falling back to legacy kernel on those pods. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 540ms, throughput down ~25%. KV cache misses up as well.

rahul (eng-sre): Heap and GPU telemetry look OK, but context-switches on canary hosts are higher. Could be batching selector or kernel affinity mismatch.

jess (deployer): We pushed a routing change + quant-kernel selector tweak in the same wave. Suggest immediate mitigation: flip canary routing off (send traffic back to control plane).

sam (oncall): Agreed. If we can revert the routing flag quickly that avoids full rollback. Maria, any customer alerts already?

maria (customer-success): Not yet automated, but support is getting inbound complaining about slow responses from users in us-west. We should prepare a proactive note if we roll back.

ting (eng-runtime): To flip feature: run:```bash
redwood-ff toggle --env prod --flag canary_route --value false --wave 4312
```
That should drain the canary pods within ~30s. Also proposing to set kernel_selector back to v1 on the canary class:```bash
orrctl set kernel_selector canary_class v1 --wave 4312
```
But second change is riskier — prefer the flag flip first.

rahul (eng-sre): I'll run the flag flip and monitor. prepping rollback plan if flips don't stabilize.

rahul (eng-sre): RUN: redwood-ff toggle --env prod --flag canary_route --value false --wave 4312 :started

deploy-bot: feature-flag update acknowledged by control plane. change propagated to 6/6 canary hosts.

ting (eng-runtime): seeing immediate drop in kernel-fallback events. p95 falling back towards 160ms. throughput recovering slowly. Good sign.

sam (oncall): How about throughput / error budgets?

ting (eng-runtime): throughput at 95% of baseline now. No increase in 5xxs. KV hit rate recovering.

maria (customer-success): Support: we patched the public status page and sent an outbound to impacted customers explaining a transient latency spike while we reverted a canary routing change. Customers asking for RCA; we'll follow up after postmortem.

jess (deployer): Given stabilization, do we still want to roll back the full wave or keep everything as-is with flag off?

ting (eng-runtime): I'd keep the code but keep canary routing off until we finish a deeper investigation into kernel selector interactions with batching heuristics and quant path. Prefer not to reintroduce risk with a full rollback if traffic is stable.

rahul (eng-sre): Agree. I'll keep the monitoring playbook on and set an alert if kernel-fallback or p95 re-elevates. Also creating a short TTL: pager escalation window 30m.

sam (oncall): Logging handoff: I'll stay on for 45m to observe, then hand to eng-runtime for post-incident followup. Assigning postmortem owner?

ting (eng-runtime): I'll own the postmortem with Rahul. We need to collect: canary host kernel logs, batching decisions, selector telemetry, and exact sequence of feature flips.

maria (customer-success): I'll coordinate customer outreach and update the affected-customer list. Please ping me when the postmortem draft is ready.

sam (oncall): Update in 15. Good work team. :thumbsup:

... 15 minutes later ...

rahul (eng-sre): Monitoring window complete. No regression after flag flip. Kernel fallback events returned to baseline. Escalation cleared.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> current_status=stabilized, mitigation=canary_route flag OFF, time_to_mitigate=00:07:43.

sam (oncall): Handoff to eng-runtime for RCA and rollout policy changes. I'll mark as resolved from oncall perspective in 45m unless anything reoccurs.

ting (eng-runtime): Next steps: reproduce in staging with same selector + batching seeds, add a defensive check before kernel_selector flips (safety guard), and run a controlled micro-canary with increased telemetry. Also propose adding a transient auto-fallback threshold to avoid mass kernel thrash.

maria (customer-success): Noted. I'll draft customer-facing note with timeline and mitigation.

jess (deployer): Logged rollback/flag action in deploy audit: release/2026.03.17-wave-4312 -> canary_route toggled off.

sam (oncall): Closing live incident thread. Postmortem to be filed in #postmortems, assign tags: cause: rollout-interaction, impact: transient-latency, mitigation: flag-off.

ting (eng-runtime): Copy. Will attach relevant traces and minimal repro.

maria (customer-success): Thank you — prepping comms.

rahul (eng-sre): resolved.

sam (oncall): closing thread. :white_check_mark:
